The California Building Code, 2025 Edition, Part 2 of Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations, consisting of two volumes, including appendices and any related errata ... is adopted and by this reference is made a part of this Code with the force and effect as though set out herein in full, with the exception of those parts expressly excepted and deleted or as amended by this chapter.

building.note: Read in the ordinance as put before the City Council for adoption on November 18, 2025 (Legistar file 25-3566; first reading file 25-3267, October 21, 2025). The copy has blanks for the ordinance number, adoption date and vote, and says it takes effect on the 30th day after adoption; the city's page gives January 1, 2026. The ordinance shows only the sections it changes. The building code amendments it shows are administrative (plan approval stamps, temporary occupancy bonds), residential noise insulation and geologic investigations; the 2022 ordinance also amended section 105.1 (when a permit may be refused) and section 903.2 (sprinklers). None concerns toilet rooms or interior finishes. Section 105.2 (work exempt from permit) is kept: it is not in the list of deleted sections and section 16.04.020 refers to 'work exempted by Section 105.2, the California Building Code'. The full current Chapter 16.08 on Municode was not read (automated access blocked). A separate 2026 ordinance added Chapter 16.15, alternative building standards for adaptive reuse projects (Legistar file 26-1933); not read.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Riverside job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Riverside warehouses, schools, college buildings and county offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Riverside uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Riverside requires a permit to alter or repair a building and follows California's list of work that needs none. The list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops, and similar finish work" and "nonfixed and movable" partitions "not over 5 feet 9 inches high". It doesn't name toilet partitions, and the city says a permit is required when work affects an accessible route, so ask the Building & Safety Division's permit counter (951-826-5800) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Riverside Building & Safety Division
page.stalls_intro: Riverside counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Riverside Building & Safety Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Riverside issues permits to licensed contractors, their representatives or owners, and a contractor needs a current City of Riverside business license. On jobs over $50,000 the applicant verifies each subcontractor's state license and city business license. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Riverside the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more and a city business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Riverside County that is $54.41 an hour plus $29.91 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.75% in Riverside: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the county transportation commission and 1% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Colleges and universities:** phenolic or solid plastic (HDPE) that stands up to heavy use between classes.
